description: Haemul Pajeon is a beloved Korean savory pancake loaded with fresh seafood and crisp green onions, offering a delightful blend of textures and flavors. Its golden-brown, crispy exterior gives way to a tender, flavorful interior, making it an irresistible appetizer or light meal. Perfectly complemented by a tangy soy-vinegar dipping sauce, this dish is a true taste of Korean culinary tradition.

ingredients.notes: shrimp, squid rings, mussels, chopped if large

instructions.title: Prepare the Dipping Sauce
instructions.text: In a small bowl, combine soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, toasted sesame seeds, and gochugaru if using. Stir well and set aside. This dipping sauce adds a fantastic tangy and savory kick to the pancake.

instructions.title: Prepare Seafood and Vegetables
instructions.text: Thaw and pat dry the assorted seafood. If using large pieces of shrimp or squid, chop them into bite-sized pieces. Wash and trim the green onions, cutting them into 3-4 inch lengths. Thinly slice the yellow onion and red chili if using. Proper preparation ensures even cooking and distribution.

instructions.title: Make the Batter
instructions.text: In a large bowl, whisk together the all-purpose flour, cornstarch, cold water, egg, and salt until a smooth batter forms. Do not overmix; a few small lumps are acceptable. Using cold water helps create a crispier pancake.

instructions.title: Combine Ingredients for the Pancake
instructions.text: Add the prepared seafood, green onions, and sliced yellow onion to the batter. Gently fold to combine, ensuring the seafood and vegetables are evenly coated with the batter. This step prepares the mix for cooking.

instructions.title: Cook the Haemul Pajeon
instructions.text: Heat 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Pour about half of the batter mixture into the skillet, spreading it evenly to form a round pancake. Arrange a few extra green onion pieces and red chili slices on top if desired. Cook for 5-7 minutes until the bottom is golden brown and crispy. Add another tablespoon of oil around the edges, then carefully flip the pancake. Cook for another 5-7 minutes on the second side until golden brown and cooked through. Repeat with the remaining batter for a second pancake.

instructions.title: Serve Immediately
instructions.text: Transfer the cooked Haemul Pajeon to a cutting board and cut into wedges. Serve immediately with the prepared dipping sauce on the side. Enjoy this crispy, savory Korean seafood pancake while it is hot for the best experience.

tips: For an extra crispy pancake, try using a mix of ice-cold water and a small amount of sparkling water in your batter. This helps create a lighter, crispier texture.
Dont overcrowd the pan. Cook one pancake at a time to ensure even cooking and a perfectly crispy exterior.
Serve Haemul Pajeon immediately after cooking, as its crispiness diminishes over time. Pair it with a cold Korean beer or makgeolli (rice wine) for an authentic experience.
article:
Haemul Pajeon: The Ultimate Guide to Korea's Savory Seafood Pancake

Imagine a sizzling hot pan, fragrant with green onions and savory seafood, yielding a pancake that’s crispy on the edges and wonderfully tender in the middle. This is the magic of Haemul Pajeon, a beloved Korean dish that has captured hearts and palates worldwide. More than just a simple pancake, Haemul Pajeon is a culinary experience – a symphony of textures and flavors that embodies the comforting essence of Korean home cooking and vibrant street food culture. Whether enjoyed on a rainy day with a glass of makgeolli (Korean rice wine) or as a communal appetizer with friends, this savory seafood pancake offers a delightful journey for your taste buds.

## What is Haemul Pajeon?

Haemul Pajeon, pronounced "heh-mool pah-jeon," literally translates to "seafood green onion pancake." At its core, it's a type of *jeon*, a broad category of Korean pan-fried dishes made from various ingredients coated in a batter and cooked on a griddle. What makes Haemul Pajeon stand out is its generous inclusion of fresh seafood and an abundance of green onions (scallions), which are the star of the dish.

Unlike sweet pancakes, Haemul Pajeon is distinctly savory, packed with umami from ingredients like shrimp, squid, mussels, and sometimes even oysters or clams. The batter, typically made from flour, water, and egg, acts as a binder, allowing the green onions to retain their slight crunch while the seafood cooks to perfection. The ideal Haemul Pajeon boasts a golden-brown, irresistibly crispy exterior that gives way to a soft, flavorful interior. It's a dish that's both hearty and refreshing, making it a popular choice in Korean restaurants, street food stalls, and family kitchens across the globe.

## Ingredients for Haemul Pajeon

Creating an authentic Haemul Pajeon requires a blend of fresh ingredients and a simple, yet effective, batter. Here’s a breakdown of what you’ll need:

For the Batter:
*   1 cup all-purpose flour (for extra crispiness, you can substitute 1/4 cup with rice flour or cornstarch)
*   1 cup cold water or anchovy broth (broth adds depth of flavor)
*   1 large egg
*   1/2 teaspoon salt
*   Pinch of black pepper

For the Pancake Filling:
*   2-3 cups green onions, cut into 3-inch lengths (the more, the better!)
*   1 cup mixed seafood, cleaned and chopped into bite-sized pieces (e.g., shrimp, squid rings, mussels, bay scallops)
*   1/2 small onion, thinly sliced (optional)
*   1/4 cup shredded carrot (optional, for color and sweetness)
*   1-2 red or green chili peppers, thinly sliced (optional, for a kick)
*   Vegetable oil, for frying

For the Dipping Sauce (basic version):
*   2 tablespoons soy sauce
*   1 tablespoon vinegar (rice vinegar or apple cider vinegar)
*   1 teaspoon sesame oil
*   1/2 teaspoon sugar
*   1 teaspoon sesame seeds
*   Pinch of gochugaru (Korean chili flakes, optional)
*   1 clove garlic, minced (optional)
*   1 tablespoon chopped green onion (optional)

## How to Make Haemul Pajeon: Step-by-Step

Making Haemul Pajeon is a straightforward process that yields incredibly rewarding results. Follow these steps for a delicious homemade treat:

1.  **Prepare the Seafood and Vegetables:** If using frozen seafood, thaw it thoroughly and pat dry. Chop shrimp and squid into bite-sized pieces. Clean mussels or scallops if necessary. Wash and trim the green onions, then cut them into 3-inch lengths. Thinly slice any optional vegetables like onion, carrot, or chili peppers.

2.  **Make the Batter:** In a large bowl, whisk together the all-purpose flour, rice flour (if using), salt, and black pepper. Gradually add the cold water or broth, whisking until just combined. Don't overmix; a few lumps are fine. Whisk in the egg until incorporated. The batter should have a consistency similar to thin pancake batter, enough to coat the ingredients without being too thick.

3.  **Combine Ingredients:** Add the prepared green onions, seafood, and any other vegetables (sliced onion, carrot, chili peppers) to the batter. Gently fold everything together until all ingredients are lightly coated.

4.  **Heat the Pan:** Heat a large non-stick frying pan or griddle over medium-high heat. Add about 2-3 tablespoons of vegetable oil, ensuring the entire surface is coated. The oil should be shimmering hot.

5.  **Cook the Pancake:** Pour about 1/2 to 1 cup of the batter mixture into the hot pan, depending on the desired size of your pancake. Spread it out evenly with a spatula to form a round, thin pancake. Arrange any visible green onion pieces or seafood nicely on top if you want a picturesque finish.

6.  **Fry to Golden Perfection:** Cook for 4-6 minutes on the first side, or until the edges are crispy and golden brown, and the batter appears cooked through. You might see bubbles forming on the surface. Add another tablespoon of oil around the edges of the pancake to ensure maximum crispiness.

7.  **Flip and Finish:** Carefully slide your spatula under the pancake and flip it over. Cook for another 3-5 minutes on the second side, or until it's also golden brown and crispy. You can gently press down on the pancake with your spatula to ensure even cooking and crispiness.

8.  **Serve:** Transfer the cooked Haemul Pajeon to a cutting board. Cut it into wedges or squares. Repeat the process with the remaining batter, adding more oil to the pan as needed for each new pancake.

## Tips for the Perfect Crispy Haemul Pajeon

Achieving that coveted crispy texture is key to an outstanding Haemul Pajeon. Here are some tips:

*   **Cold Batter:** Using cold water or broth for the batter helps prevent gluten development, resulting in a lighter, crispier pancake.
*   **Don't Overmix:** Overmixing develops gluten, leading to a chewy, rather than crispy, texture. A few lumps are perfectly acceptable.
*   **Plenty of Oil:** Don't be shy with the oil! It's crucial for frying the pancake to a beautiful golden crisp. Add more oil when you flip the pancake.
*   **Hot Pan:** Ensure your pan is hot before adding the batter. This creates an immediate sear, preventing the pancake from absorbing too much oil and becoming greasy.
*   **Thin is In:** Spread the batter thinly. Thicker pancakes tend to be doughier, while thinner ones crisp up better.
*   **Generous Green Onions:** The green onions aren't just for flavor; their structure contributes to the pancake's overall texture.
*   **Rice Flour or Starch:** A small amount of rice flour or cornstarch in the batter can significantly enhance the crispiness.
*   **Cook in Batches:** Don't overcrowd the pan. Cook one or two pancakes at a time to maintain consistent heat and ensure even cooking.

## Serving Suggestions & Dipping Sauce

Haemul Pajeon is best enjoyed immediately, hot off the pan. Cut it into bite-sized wedges or squares for easy sharing. While delicious on its own, it truly shines when paired with a tangy and savory dipping sauce.

**Basic Dipping Sauce Recipe:**
Combine 2 tablespoons soy sauce, 1 tablespoon vinegar, 1 teaspoon sesame oil, 1/2 teaspoon sugar, 1 teaspoon sesame seeds, and a pinch of gochugaru (Korean chili flakes) if you like a little heat. For extra flavor, add a minced clove of garlic and a tablespoon of finely chopped green onion. Mix well.

**Serving Pairings:**
*   **Makgeolli:** Traditionally, Haemul Pajeon is enjoyed with makgeolli, a milky, slightly sweet Korean rice wine, especially on rainy days.
*   **Beer:** A cold beer also makes an excellent companion, cutting through the richness of the pancake.
*   **Other Banchan:** Serve alongside other Korean side dishes like kimchi, pickled radishes, or seasoned bean sprouts for a complete meal experience.

## Variations and Dietary Substitutions

The versatility of the jeon category means you can easily adapt Haemul Pajeon to suit different tastes and dietary needs:

*   **Vegetarian Pajeon (Yachaejeon):** Omit the seafood entirely and load up on vegetables. Mushrooms (shiitake, oyster), zucchini, bell peppers, onions, and carrots all work wonderfully. You can also add kimchi for a *Kimchi Pajeon* (Kimchijeon), which is another popular variation.
*   **Different Seafood:** Feel free to customize the seafood mix based on your preference and what's available. Clams, oysters, or even crab meat can be excellent additions.
*   **Gluten-Free:** For a gluten-free version, use a gluten-free all-purpose flour blend or solely rice flour for the batter. Ensure all other ingredients are also gluten-free.
*   **Spicy Kick:** Increase the amount of chili peppers in the batter or add a teaspoon of gochujang (Korean chili paste) for a bolder flavor.
*   **Broth Base:** Instead of plain water, use dashi (kelp and anchovy broth) or vegetable broth in the batter for an added layer of umami.

Haemul Pajeon is more than just a dish; it's a celebration of simple, fresh ingredients transformed into something truly special. Its irresistible crispiness, savory depth, and comforting warmth make it a perennial favorite. Don't hesitate to experiment with the ingredients and find your perfect version of this iconic Korean seafood pancake. Enjoy the process, and savor every delicious bite!
